title: Supported exterior products respect localization triangles
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, $A$ a finite commutative ring, and $X,Y$ schemes [def-pc-scheme] of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], separated in the diagonal sense [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Closed subschemes mean closed immersions [def-weil-closed-immersion], and products are fibre products over $k$ [def-pc-base-change]. Write $p_X:X\times_kY\to X$ and $p_Y:X\times_kY\to Y$ for the projections. Let $B,C\subseteq X$ and $D\subseteq Y$ be closed subschemes, set $U=X\setminus C$, and let $K\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and $L\in D^+(Y_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ with $F=p_X^*K\otimes_A^Lp_Y^*L$ bounded below. Use sections with support as in [def-pur-support-cohomology], derived tensor as in [def-kun-derived-tensor], and the supported exterior products of [def-pur-supported-exterior-product]. The three supported exterior-product maps
$$
\begin{aligned}
R\Gamma_{B\cap C}(X,K)\otimes_A^LR\Gamma_D(Y,L)&\longrightarrow R\Gamma_{(B\cap C)\times_kD}(X\times_kY,F),\\
R\Gamma_B(X,K)\otimes_A^LR\Gamma_D(Y,L)&\longrightarrow R\Gamma_{B\times_kD}(X\times_kY,F),\\
R\Gamma_{B\cap U}(U,K|_U)\otimes_A^LR\Gamma_D(Y,L)&\longrightarrow R\Gamma_{(B\cap U)\times_kD}(U\times_kY,F|_{U\times_kY})
\end{aligned}
$$
form a morphism of distinguished triangles [def-weil-triangulated-category] in $D(A)$, the unbounded derived category of $A$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]: the top row is the support-restriction triangle [lem-pur-support-restriction-triangle] for $(X,B,C,K)$ tensored with $R\Gamma_D(Y,L)$ and the bottom row is the support-restriction triangle for $(X\times_kY,B\times_kD,C\times_kY,F)$. In particular the square with the connecting morphisms commutes, using the shift identification of the exact tensor functor. The diagrams are natural under open restriction of either ambient scheme and under morphisms of $K,L$. Explicitly, for closed subschemes $D'\subseteq X$ and $B',C'\subseteq Y$, put $V=Y\setminus C'$. The three components
$$
\kappa^{D',B'\cap C'}_{K,L},\qquad
\kappa^{D',B'}_{K,L},\qquad
\kappa^{D',B'\cap V}_{K,L|_V}
$$
form a morphism from the support-restriction triangle for $(Y,B',C',L)$ tensored on the left with $R\Gamma_{D'}(X,K)$ to the support-restriction triangle for $(X\times_kY,D'\times_kB',X\times_kC',F)$. The third target term has ambient scheme $X\times_kV$. The boundary square uses the left-tensor shift identification $M\otimes_A^LN[1]\cong(M\otimes_A^LN)[1]$, represented on total tensor complexes by $x\otimes y\mapsto(-1)^{\deg(x)}x\otimes y$. The first-variable boundary uses $M[1]\otimes_A^LN\cong(M\otimes_A^LN)[1]$, represented by $x\otimes y\mapsto x\otimes y$. No assertion that any exterior-product map is invertible is made.

source.place: Tag 09XP, section-cohomology-support, the injective restriction sequence and its derived triangle; Tag 0F1E, remark-define-kunneth-map. Compatibility of the supported pairing and connecting morphisms is an agent-formulated refinement of these constructions.

proof.text: The fibre products and projections in the statement are the base changes supplied by [def-pc-base-change]. Pulling the closed immersions defining B, C, and D back along the projections gives the closed supports (B∩C)×ₖD, B×ₖD, and (B∩U)×ₖD; pulling back the open complement U gives U×ₖY. These identifications are immediate on affine charts from the fibre-product and closed-immersion definitions, and they also identify the analogous products D′×ₖB′, X×ₖC′ and X×ₖV in the second-variable formulation. More explicitly, on $\operatorname{Spec}R\times_k\operatorname{Spec}S$, the product of supports defined by $I\subset R$ and $J\subset S$ is defined by the sum of their extended ideals in $R\otimes_kS$. The intersection $B\cap C$ is defined by $I_B+I_C$, so both descriptions of its product with $D$ give the ideal generated by $I_B,I_C,I_D$. Taking the complement of the extended ideal of $C$ gives exactly $U\times_kY$.

Put N=RΓ_D(Y,L). By [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor] with R=A, the operation E↦E⊗ᴸ_A N is an everywhere-defined exact functor of derived categories, computed by K-flat models and canonical under changes of model. Apply this functor to the support-restriction triangle for (X,B,C,K) supplied by [lem-pur-support-restriction-triangle]. The resulting distinguished triangle has exactly the three source objects displayed in the first row of the statement.

source.place: Tag 06Y6 (lemma-derived-base-change); exact tensor functor on the one-point site

proof.text: Use coefficient sheaves to specify the resolution diagram. For a closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ put $S_Z=i_*A_Z$, with $A_Z$ the constant coefficient sheaf. For a bounded-below injective representative $I$ of $H$ supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative], the complex $\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}_T(S_Z,I)$ computes $R\Gamma_Z(T,H)$. Indeed [lem-weil-pbc-open-closed-short-exact] for $A_T$ gives $0\to j_!A_{T\setminus Z}\to A_T\to S_Z\to0$. Applying $\operatorname{Hom}_T(-,I^n)$ is exact because $I^n$ is injective. By [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction], its first kernel is exactly $\ker(I^n(T)\to I^n(T\setminus Z))=\Gamma_Z(T,I^n)$. These identifications commute with differentials. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective] gives the asserted complex-level supported-Hom identification. Here and below global Hom complexes mean sections of the Hom complex of [def-pur-hom-complex]; a K-injective second argument is the derived Hom convention of [def-pur-derived-internal-hom].

source.place: Tag 09XP (section-cohomology-support); Tag 095L (lemma-ses-associated-to-open); supported-Hom model of the kernel of restriction

proof.text: For $j:U\hookrightarrow X$, set $E_0=S_{B\cap C}$, $E_1=S_B$, and $E_2=j_!S_{B\cap U}$, where the last support sheaf is formed on $U$. There is a coefficient sequence $0\to E_2\to E_1\to E_0\to0$: apply [lem-weil-pbc-open-closed-short-exact] to $E_1$ and the pair $(C,U)$. Its closed term is $S_{B\cap C}$ and its open term is $j_!S_{B\cap U}$. To check these identifications, a closed immersion is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-finite], so [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-stalk-formula] and [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-geometric-stalk] identify $(S_Z)_{\bar t}$ with $A$ on $Z$ and $0$ off $Z$. Pullback of these stalks is given by [lem-weil-pbc-global-sections-stalk-comparison]. The maps are restriction of constant sections, hence are the identity on the nonzero stalks. Stalk conservativity [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] identifies the closed and open terms, the latter also by the counit and the defining extension-by-zero presheaf [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero]. Every $S_Z$ is flat: by [lem-pod-etale-stalk-tensor-scalar], tensoring has stalk either tensor with $A$ or tensor with $0$, and [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact] and stalk conservativity detect exactness. The open term $E_2$ is flat as well: at a point on $C$ the stalk of $E_1\to E_0$ is the identity, and off $C$ its target is zero, so its kernel has stalk either $0$ or $A$. Consequently the $E_i$ and their bounded mapping cones are K-flat by [lem-kun-kflat-criteria]. On $P=X\times_kY$ the sequence $p_X^*E_2\otimes_Ap_Y^*S_D\to p_X^*E_1\otimes_Ap_Y^*S_D\to p_X^*E_0\otimes_Ap_Y^*S_D$ is short exact, using exact inverse image [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] and flatness. Multiplication of pulled-back constant sections identifies its terms with $j_{P!}S_{(B\cap U)\times_kD}$, $S_{B\times_kD}$ and $S_{(B\cap C)\times_kD}$: on each geometric stalk this is $A\otimes_A A\to A$ on the indicated product support and the map between zero modules elsewhere. Thus this is the product coefficient sequence, including its specified maps.

source.place: Tag 095L (lemma-ses-associated-to-open); Tag 04FX (lemma-stalk-pushforward-closed-immersion); coefficient support sequence and its external tensor product

proof.text:
The derived pairing may now be evaluated on this coefficient sequence, rather than on an unspecified completion of two squares. Write $\mathsf H_T(E,H)=R\operatorname{Hom}_T(E,H)$ for the global Hom complex defined in step 3. For a coefficient complex $E$ on $X$, pull back the evaluation maps $E\otimes_A^L\mathsf H_X(E,K)\to K$ and $S_D\otimes_A^L\mathsf H_Y(S_D,L)\to L$, and tensor them. Using [lem-kun-inverse-image-monoidal] and the exact module inverse image of [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], their adjoint is a pairing
$$\lambda_E:\mathsf H_X(E,K)\otimes_A^L\mathsf H_Y(S_D,L)\longrightarrow\mathsf H_P(p_X^*E\otimes_A^Lp_Y^*S_D,F).$$
The adjunction used here is the elementary Hom–tensor bijection on complexes: a map from an $A$-complex $Q$ to $\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}_X(E,I)$ is the same as a map $\underline Q\otimes_A E\to I$, obtained by evaluation on each homogeneous tensor with the Koszul sign; its inverse curries that map. Taking a K-flat model of $Q$ and a K-injective model of $K$ gives this bijection after localization. For the flat bounded coefficient complexes and cones of step 4, [lem-pur-hom-kflat-into-kinjective] ensures that their sheaf Hom into a K-injective complex is itself K-injective, so its global sections represent the global derived Hom used here. This is the derived evaluation construction: on Hom complexes homogeneous maps $f,g$ act by $(e\otimes d)\mapsto(-1)^{\deg(g)\deg(e)}f(e)\otimes g(d)$. Its compatibility with the Hom differential follows from $d(f)=d_Kf-(-1)^{\deg f}f d_E$ [def-pur-hom-complex] and the tensor differential [def-kun-derived-tensor]. It is compatible with cones in the contravariant coefficient argument, including the last map: a cone has the two summands $E'\oplus E[1]$ and differential with off-diagonal entry the coefficient map [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]; evaluation on either summand is the displayed formula, and its commutation with that off-diagonal entry is precisely precomposition naturality of $f$. Projection to the shifted summand gives the boundary square. This calculation descends to the derived pairing using the K-flat resolutions of [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], the model independence in [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor], and the K-injective Hom convention [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]; cone identifications are made before localization, so the third component is the specified derived evaluation map. Under step 3 and the coefficient identifications of step 4, $\lambda_{E_0},\lambda_{E_1},\lambda_{E_2}$ are the three maps of [def-pur-supported-exterior-product]: evaluation at $1$ in each constant support sheaf sends the two supported sections to their pulled-back tensor. This identifies the maps themselves, not just their compositions after forgetting support.

source.place: Tag 08J7 (section-internal-hom), Tag 0A8X (section-hom-complexes), Tag 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product); derived evaluation and the explicit cone calculation

proof.text: Applying $\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}_X(-,I)$ to the coefficient sequence in step 4 gives the degreewise short exact sequence $0\to\Gamma_{B\cap C}(X,I)\to\Gamma_B(X,I)\to\Gamma_{B\cap U}(U,I|_U)\to0$: step 3 identifies its first two complexes, and [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction] identifies the third. Restriction of $I$ to $U$ is injective by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-restriction-injectives], with $j$ etale by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale]. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective] identifies its third complex with the required derived sections. The product coefficient sequence gives exactly the corresponding product sequence by the same Hom-kernel identification of step 3, applied on $P$; its terms are those listed in step 4, with open ambient scheme $U\times_kY$. By [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle], these coefficient-Hom triangles have the actual connecting maps of [lem-pur-support-restriction-triangle]. Step 5 gives a morphism between these triangles after exact derived tensoring, so it proves the boundary square for the specified three exterior products. No claim that tensoring an arbitrary injective section complex is exact is needed: on complexes of ordinary $A$-modules one may resolve the fixed tensor factor by a K-flat complex with flat terms [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], and the direct-sum total tensor then preserves the degreewise short exact sequence, because every summand is tensor with a flat module.

source.place: Tag 0152 (lemma-derived-canonical-delta-functor); identify the coefficient-Hom sequence with the support-restriction sequence and its boundary

proof.text: On a total tensor complex the differential on a (p,q)-summand is d_E⊗1+(-1)^p1⊗d_F, by [def-kun-derived-tensor]. The canonical identification N[1]⊗ᴸ_A M≅(N⊗ᴸ_A M)[1] therefore sends x⊗y to x⊗y, whereas M⊗ᴸ_A N[1]≅(M⊗ᴸ_A N)[1] sends x⊗y to (-1)^{deg(x)}x⊗y. These are the shift identifications used in the boundary square; the displayed formulas follow by checking the two differentials on homogeneous tensors. This also shows that no sign is hidden in the first-variable formulation. Explicitly, for $x\in M^{p+1}$ regarded as degree $p$ in $M[1]$, the source differential on $x\otimes y$ is $-d_Mx\otimes y+(-1)^p x\otimes d_Ny$, which is the differential of $(M\otimes N)[1]$. For $x\in M^p$ and $y\in N^{q+1}$ regarded as degree $q$ in $N[1]$, the source differential is $d_Mx\otimes y-(-1)^p x\otimes d_Ny$; multiplying by $(-1)^p$ in the target, and by $(-1)^{p+1}$ on the $d_Mx$ term, yields exactly the negative total differential in the shifted target.

source.place: Tag 06YU (definition-derived-tor), with its preceding construction and following sign-symmetry paragraph; direct computation with the total tensor differential and cochain shift

proof.text: For the second-variable clause put $V=Y\setminus C'$, $N=R\Gamma_{D'}(X,K)$ and $E'_0=S_{B'\cap C'}$, $E'_1=S_{B'}$, $E'_2=j_{V!}S_{B'\cap V}$ on $Y$. The sequence $0\to E'_2\to E'_1\to E'_0\to0$ is [lem-weil-pbc-open-closed-short-exact] for $S_{B'}$ and $(C',V)$; its stalk maps are the identity on $B'\cap C'$ and zero off that support, as verified in step 4. Tensoring its pullback to $P$ with $p_X^*S_{D'}$ gives the product coefficient sequence with terms $j_{X\times V,!}S_{D'\times(B'\cap V)}$, $S_{D'\times B'}$, and $S_{D'\times(B'\cap C')}$. Apply the evaluation construction of step 5 with the fixed first coefficient sheaf $S_{D'}$ and the varying second coefficient $E'$. Evaluation at constant sections gives respectively $\kappa^{D',B'\cap C'}_{K,L}$, $\kappa^{D',B'}_{K,L}$ and $\kappa^{D',B'\cap V}_{K,L|_V}$ [def-pur-supported-exterior-product]; the off-diagonal entry of a cone is now in the second tensor factor, so the total differential contributes $(-1)^{\deg(x)}$, exactly the second shift identification calculated in step 7. Applying Hom to the two coefficient sequences identifies the rows with [lem-pur-support-restriction-triangle] on $Y$ and on $P$ by step 6 and [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle]. The left tensor functor is exact: the degreewise symmetry $x\otimes y\mapsto(-1)^{\deg(x)\deg(y)}y\otimes x$ from [def-kun-derived-tensor] identifies it with the right tensor functor of [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor] (the sign commutes with the total differential and carries K-flat quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms). This is the entire second-variable morphism, including its boundary square and its third ambient scheme $X\times_kV$.

source.place: Tag 09XP (section-cohomology-support), Tag 095L (lemma-ses-associated-to-open), Tag 0F1E (remark-define-kunneth-map); explicit second-variable coefficient sequence and evaluation

proof.text: For morphisms of $K$ and $L$, the two evaluation composites both send a tensor of supported sections $s\otimes t$ to $p_X^*\alpha(s)\otimes p_Y^*\beta(t)$. For an open restriction $X_0\hookrightarrow X$, they both send it to $p_{X_0}^*(s|_{X_0})\otimes p_Y^*t$; restricting $Y$ gives $p_X^*s\otimes p_{Y_0}^*(t|_{Y_0})$. These identities hold degreewise for Hom evaluation and commute with the coefficient sequence maps, hence with the cone maps of step 5. The derived Hom construction [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] and K-flat model independence [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor] pass these identities through localization at quasi-isomorphisms: for a roof they hold for its numerator and denominator and hence after the denominator is inverted. The diagrams and their boundaries are therefore natural for the stated restrictions and coefficient morphisms.
